name: RoboHarm
summary: Introduces a benchmark of harmful robot instructions and evaluates frontier models under a fixed-model design, in which the interface varies across text, Code as Policies, and vision agents commanding end-effector poses or joint angles.
numbers: 7 models; refusal 73% in text, 18–25% in control; real YAM arm: 18% of 612 trials (end-effector), 41% of 252 (joint)

why.dex: Model commands poses or joints directly on a bimanual arm.
why.cog: Must infer the harm of an action from the scene; refusals hinge on object uncertainty.
